items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the real property tax law, in relation to an exemption of capital improvements to certain residential buildings within certain cities
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7847

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the real property tax law, in relation to an exemption
of capital improvements to certain residential buildings within
certain cities

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To provide cities with a population of more than ten-thousand
inhabitants and fewer than twelve thousand inhabitants the authority
to pass a local law authorizing a real property tax exemption program
that exempts from taxation the additional valuation for capital
improvements to certain residential single and multi-family
properties.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Amends the real property tax law by adding a new section 421-o. This
legislation would authorize, at the city of Coming's option, to pass a
local resolution authorizing a 12-year real property tax exemption
program for single and multiple dwelling residences that are
renovated, reconstructed and given general improvements. The exemption
covers the increase in assessment value of such properties resulting
from reconstruction, alteration, and improvements. The dollar increase
in assessed value in the initial year shall be referred to as an
"exemption base." Qualifying residential units will be entitled to a
100% tax exemption for the value of such improvements one year after
the assessment increase, and the exemption shall decrease by 8.3% of
the original "exemption base" over the subsequent 11 years. The
criteria for eligibility pertaining to the nature of the
reconstruction, alteration, and improvements are contained within the
provisions of the bill.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This legislation will allow for the city of Corning, at their option,
to embark upon an organized effort to rehabilitate portions of the
city where certain single and multi-family residential dwellings have
fallen into disrepair. This program will provide property owners who
renovate, rehabilitate and make improvements to these properties a
12-year tax exemption from the increased assessed value of these
improvements, with such exemption tapering off for a period of 12
years subsequent to obtaining approval by the city. This will help
ease the financial burden on individuals who are interesting in
rehabilitating these residential units within the city, thus helping
contribute to a broader series of efforts the city has embarked upon
to revitalize the area. In particular, many multi-family residential
units end up with major wear and tear, and are therefore in need of
substantial rehabilitation.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

This is a new bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the first of January next succeeding the
date this bill shall have become law.
